newsitem.title: INDONESIA: KFC Holdings buys into Sierad.
newsitem.headline: KFC Holdings buys into Sierad.

text.p: Malaysian integrated poultry and fast food chain KFC Holdings (Malaysia) Bhd has agreed to buy 50 million shares, or 6.78 percent, of Indonesia's PT Sierad Produce, Sierad said in a statement on Friday.
The deal would be worth 45 billion rupiah ($19 million), according to Sierad's closing share price on Friday at 900 rupiah.
Sierad said KFC's investment represented "a first step in forging a strategic alliance".

It said the two companies had many similarities in their core businesses and the alliance would increase possibilities for future developments in both Indonesia and Malaysia. Sierad officials were not immediately available to comment further.
According to Jakarta stock exchange records on February 13, Sierad had 737.84 million shares listed.
KFC Holdings is the Malaysian franchise holder of PepsiCo's Kentucky Fried Chicken.
